metaDescription: A photo editing prompt is the instruction you give an AI tool to change a photo. Copy one below, paste it into Gemini or ChatGPT, and edit in seconds.
bodyHtml:
A photo editing prompt is a short written instruction you paste into an AI tool along with your photo. It tells the AI exactly what to change: the lighting, the background, the outfit, the style. A clear one gets you a usable edit in one or two tries. A vague one wastes your evening.

The prompts on this page work in Gemini, ChatGPT, Midjourney's editor, and most other image tools. Copy one, upload your photo, paste, and adjust a word or two until it fits.

Why the wording matters more than the tool

People blame the AI when an edit comes back looking wrong. Nine times out of ten the prompt was the problem. 'Make my photo better' gives the model nothing to work with, so it guesses. 'Brighten the shadows on my face, keep the background unchanged' gives it a job it can actually do.

The models are good now. Gemini and ChatGPT can both retouch skin, swap backgrounds, relight a scene, and restyle clothes from a single photo. What they cannot do is read your mind.

The four parts of a photo editing prompt that works

  1. The change. Name one main edit. 'Change the background to a plain studio grey.' One prompt, one job. Stack a second prompt for a second change.
  2. The keep line. Say what must not change. 'Keep my face, hairstyle, and expression exactly the same.' Without this, AI tools drift, and you stop looking like you.
  3. The look. Describe the finish: 'soft natural light', 'warm golden-hour glow', 'clean magazine retouch'. This is where the style lives.
  4. The format. If it matters, say so: portrait crop, square for Instagram, sharp focus on the eyes.
Write the keep line before the look line. If you only remember one rule from this page, make it that one.

Photo editing prompt examples by job

Edit you wantWording to try
Cleaner portrait'Retouch this photo lightly: even out skin tone, reduce shine, keep pores and texture real. Keep my face unchanged.'
New background'Replace the background with a soft, blurred city street at dusk. Match the lighting on me to the new scene. Keep my face and clothes the same.'
Better lighting'Relight this photo with warm window light from the left, gentle shadows, natural skin tones. Keep everything else unchanged.'
Outfit change'Change my outfit to a plain black formal suit. Keep my face, pose, and background exactly as they are.'
Old photo repair'Restore this old photo: remove scratches and dust, fix faded colors, sharpen gently. Do not change any faces.'
Film look'Grade this photo like 35mm film: soft grain, slightly faded blacks, warm highlights. Keep the framing unchanged.'

Which tool should you paste it into?

For editing your own photos, Gemini is the easiest starting point. Its image model handles face-preserving edits well, and there is a free tier. We keep a separate page of Gemini photo editing prompts tuned for it.

ChatGPT is the better talker. You can go back and forth: 'a bit warmer', 'less blur', 'try again with shorter hair'. If that is your style, start with our ChatGPT photo editing prompts.

Midjourney gives the most stylised results but is the least literal about keeping faces. Use it for artistic edits, not for photos where you need to stay recognisable.

When the edit comes back wrong

The face changed

Your keep line was missing or too weak. Add 'keep my exact face, do not alter facial features' and try again. If it still drifts, cut some style words. Strong style words fight the keep line, and the style words usually win.

It looks plastic

The model over-retouched. Ask for less: 'light retouch only, keep real skin texture, no smoothing'. Words like 'flawless' and 'perfect' are what cause the wax-figure look, so leave them out.

It ignored half the request

You asked for too much in one go. Split the prompt: background first, then lighting, then the outfit. Each pass stays accurate because the model only has one thing to think about.

Reusing one prompt across many photos

Once a prompt works, save it and treat it as a template. The structure carries over; only the specifics change. 'Replace the background with X, match the lighting, keep my face the same' works whether X is a beach, an office, or a wedding stage. Most people who edit photos with AI every week rely on five or six saved prompts and swap the details.

faqs.q: What is a photo editing prompt?
faqs.a: It is the written instruction you give an AI tool together with your photo. It names the change you want (background, lighting, outfit, retouch), what must stay the same, and the style of the finish. The AI applies the edit to your image based on those words.

faqs.q: Which AI tool is best for photo editing prompts?
faqs.a: Gemini is the easiest for face-preserving edits of your own photos and has a free tier. ChatGPT is better if you like refining an edit over several messages. Midjourney suits artistic restyling more than faithful editing. The prompts on this page work in all three with minor tweaks.

faqs.q: How do I write a photo editing prompt that keeps my face the same?
faqs.a: Add an explicit keep line: 'keep my face, features, and expression exactly the same.' Put it right after the change you are asking for, and keep style words moderate. If the face still drifts, remove style words one at a time until it holds.

faqs.q: Are these photo editing prompts free to use?
faqs.a: Yes. Every prompt on this page is free to copy, and there is no signup. Gemini and ChatGPT both offer free tiers that handle a reasonable number of image edits per day.

faqs.q: Why does my edit look fake or plastic?
faqs.a: The model over-smoothed the skin, which usually happens when a prompt asks for a 'perfect' or 'flawless' result. Ask for a light retouch instead and tell it to keep real skin texture. Natural beats perfect in nearly every photo.
